mechanisms.name: Security regression: v1.11.5 is newer than v1.12.0 (1.11.5 security fixes #13070 absent from 1.12.0)
mechanisms.mechanism: Moving from 4.11.5 (v1.11.5) to 4.12.0 (v1.12.0) goes backwards in patch level. The 1.11.5 changelog has 'Controller: Several security fixes (#13070)' and the 1.12.0 changelog has no such entry, so the upgrade would drop those fixes. From memory (not from the repo), the #13070 fixes are the March 2025 admission-webhook CVE batch (CVE-2025-1974 and related). Because the admission webhook is enabled, the exposure would apply here.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: No mitigation within 1.12.0. The assessment suggests targeting a later 1.12.x (v1.12.1 through v1.12.8 are listed as later releases) or 1.13/1.14, or moving off ingress-nginx. It notes the project is retired (best-effort maintenance only until March 2026), so no further fixes are coming.
citedEvidence: README support table listing v1.12.1 through v1.12.8
README: project retired, best-effort maintenance until March 2026
assumptions: The link between #13070 and CVE-2025-1974 and related CVEs comes from memory, not from the repo; it needs verifying against the advisory
missingEvidence: The advisory for the #13070 fixes and the actual fix versions
recommendedValidation: Check the advisory for the #13070 fixes and the real fix versions
Decide whether to target a later 1.12.x or newer release, or a replacement, instead of 1.12.0 (the main blocker)

mechanisms.name: Chart downgrades the kube-webhook-certgen helper image (v1.5.2 -> v1.5.0)
resourcesConsumers: kube-webhook-certgen Jobs (Helm hooks / Argo PreSync hooks)
mechanisms.mechanism: The 4.11.5 chart carries the later certgen bump (#13067, #12697), and 4.12.0 predates it, so the certgen image moves from v1.5.2 back to v1.5.0.
missingEvidence: Whether the cluster's scanner or admission policy accepts the older certgen image
Whether the certgen hooks re-run cleanly with the older image against the existing webhook secret
recommendedValidation: Check the cluster's scanner or admission policy for the older certgen image
Run the full Argo sync in staging, including the certgen hooks and webhook CA patch

mechanisms.name: Strict path-type validation on by default (strict-validate-path-type)
resourcesConsumers: wellknown pod serving security.txt from a ConfigMap mounted at /usr/share/nginx/html/.well-known
mechanisms.mechanism: Strict validation of Exact/Prefix paths could reject the Ingress paths. If the path were rejected, the failure would be silent and public-facing. With the webhook enabled, a changed Ingress would be rejected at apply time. An existing Ingress that is not re-applied would instead be rejected or ignored when the controller syncs it. Either way the /.well-known URLs could stop working or fall through to docs-site.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: As the assessment remembers it, the validation only allows alphanumerics and '. _ - /' in Exact/Prefix paths, and '.well-known' contains only those characters. '/' is ubiquitous, so it is expected to be accepted. The 1.12.0 changelog does not touch ingress-nginx path matching itself; the only risk is the new strict validation.
assumptions: The allowed character set is recalled from memory; the validator source is not in the repo and the exact regex has not been confirmed
'/' is expected to be accepted because it is ubiquitous
apps/docs is the only Ingress, as the orientation states
missingEvidence: Confirmation that apps/docs is really the only Ingress in prod
recommendedValidation: On a non-prod cluster running v1.12.0, run kubectl apply --dry-run=server on the rendered docs Ingress, then curl /, /.well-known/security.txt and /index.html
Look at the controller logs for validation errors
Run kubectl get ingress -A -o yaml on prod to verify that apps/docs is the only Ingress

mechanisms.name: Annotation validation on, risk level lowered to High
mechanisms.mechanism: Annotation validation with a lowered risk level could reject high or critical risk annotations.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The only annotation is ssl-redirect: "false", which is low risk. No snippet or other high or critical annotations exist anywhere in env/.
assumptions: apps/docs is the only Ingress (the repo is declared complete)
missingEvidence: Prod check that no stray Ingress uses a snippet
recommendedValidation: Run kubectl get ingress -A -o yaml to verify that apps/docs is the only Ingress

missingEvidence: Prod check for a stray Ingress using a cross-namespace secret
recommendedValidation: Run kubectl get ingress -A -o yaml to verify that apps/docs is the only Ingress

mechanisms.name: Metrics disabled by default (--enable-metrics)

mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The chart already rendered --enable-metrics=false for 4.11.5 because controller.metrics.enabled defaults to false, so dropping the flag is equivalent. No ServiceMonitor or metrics values exist in env/.
missingEvidence: Whether anything outside the repo scrapes the controller (unknown)
recommendedValidation: Check for external Prometheus, dashboards or alerts that depend on controller metrics, and whether anything scrapes the controller and expects metrics to be on

mechanisms.name: Image contents and binary defaults change (Alpine 3.20 -> 3.21, NGINX base 1.1.0, inlined Lua removed from template)
mechanisms.mechanism: Unchanged manifests do not prove runtime compatibility: the image contents change and the defaults baked into the binary change.
missingEvidence: Runtime verification (no cluster access was available)

mechanisms.name: Controller runAsGroup: 82 (and runAsGroup: 65532 on certgen jobs)
mechanisms.mechanism: The new group setting could affect files that the nginx user (UID 101) must write at runtime.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Those files are normally owned by 101. 'I believe the group change is harmless, but it is untested here.' The image is non-root with readOnlyRootFilesystem: false.
assumptions: The group change is believed harmless but untested
recommendedValidation: not stated

mechanisms.name: Rollout with externalTrafficPolicy: Local
mechanisms.mechanism: During the rolling update, a node could briefly have zero ready controller pods while the load balancer still sends it traffic.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The controller runs 2 replicas, so a rolling update is possible.
recommendedValidation: Check that no node briefly has zero ready controller pods while the LB still sends it traffic
Run a rollout rehearsal in staging and watch for 5xx errors during the controller rollout

mechanisms.name: Rollback
mechanisms.mechanism: On rollback, the ConfigMap, flags and certgen image would flip again.
recommendedValidation: not stated

overall.recommendation: Do not proceed as framed. No documented breaking change appears to break this environment (based on static evidence only), but 1.12.0 moves backwards in patch level and loses the 1.11.5 security fixes. The assessment recommends targeting a later 1.12.x or 1.13/1.14 release, or moving off ingress-nginx, after confirming the security status (the main blocker) and running the listed tests.
overall.quote: The upgrade is not recommended as framed, though, because it moves backwards in patch level.
